statement: A map $h(x)=\frac{ax+b}{cx+d}$. (i) Show that $h$ is its own inverse (assuming it is not the identity) precisely when $a+d=0$. (ii) For $h(x)=\frac{2x+1}{x-2}$, verify it is self-inverse. (iii) Find its fixed points.
solution: (i) $h(h(x))=x$ means the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ squares to a scalar multiple of the identity. Computing, $h(h(x))=\frac{(a^{2}+bc)x+b(a+d)}{c(a+d)x+(bc+d^{2})}$. For this to equal $x$ identically we need $c(a+d)=0$ and $b(a+d)=0$ and $a^{2}+bc=bc+d^{2}$. If $a+d\neq0$ then $b=c=0$ and $a^{2}=d^{2}$, giving $h(x)=a/d$; self-inverse forces $a/d=-1$, i.e. $a+d=0$ again. So the required condition is $a+d=0$. (ii) $h(h(x))=\frac{2\frac{2x+1}{x-2}+1}{\frac{2x+1}{x-2}-2}=\frac{4x+2+x-2}{2x+1-2x+4}=\frac{5x}{5}=x$. (iii) $\frac{2x+1}{x-2}=x\Rightarrow x^{2}-4x-1=0$, so $x=2\pm\sqrt{5}$.
hints: Compose h with itself and compare with x.
